Spider Solitaire · Objective-C → Unity port

iPhone 7 — Unity Port Fidelity

Unity 8.0.0  vs  Obj-C 7.42.5  ·  750×1334  ·  15 screens  ·  second Unity build

This second Unity build clears five defects from the previous pass — the empty FAQ, the duplicated Help “Introduction”, the missing About divider, and both spelling typos are all fixed. It is still not pixel-faithful on iPhone 7 though: every screen deviates, the FAQ now loads the wrong game’s content, the main-menu promo strip is still dropped, and systemic typography drift shifts text throughout. Drag any image to wipe between the builds; switch to Diff for the exact changed pixels (red).

Findings · triage

Grouped for the porting team, most actionable first.

  • Content bug
    FAQ shows the wrong game’s contentFAQ

    The FAQ is now populated (it was blank in the previous Unity build) but lists Klondike / regular-Solitaire questions — “draw 1 card to 3 cards”, “Yellow Triangle” — instead of Spider’s own (“why can’t I move a pile”, “play with more than one suit”, “undo a move”). Wrong content source wired in.

  • Dropped element
    Cross-promo icon strip still missingMenu

    The main menu’s left strip of 5 cross-promo game icons — and the “More Games” unread badge — are still absent in Unity.

  • Layout drift
    Victory screens recolored & restyledVictory

    The help / new / stats buttons are blue in Unity vs Obj-C’s red, and Victory · Score gains a top promo-icon strip that the Obj-C first-win screen doesn’t show.

  • Layout drift
    Systemic typography driftsystemic

    Unity renders body text heavier and wraps lines differently, so text shifts even where the words match — the main driver of the Help / Options / FAQ diffs. Also: Difficulty picker adds “More Games”/“Choose Look” + drops the smiley cursor; More Games art sits lower; card-back grid reordered; Stats markers “*” vs “✻”.

  • Fixed
    Fixed since the previous Unity buildregression check

    Five earlier defects are resolved: the empty FAQ now renders, Help no longer duplicates its “Introduction”, the About title’s “▷” divider is restored, and the “feeback” → “feedback” and “syymbols” → “symbols” typos are corrected.

Screen by screen

Ranked by pixel difference, worst first. Status bar, ad banner, the randomly-dealt cards, and the victory screens’ run-dependent score block are masked so the numbers reflect UI, not chrome or game state. Statistics is not apples-to-apples — games were played on the Unity device, so its values differ from the fresh-install baseline.
